archimate:Deliverable.name: technology strategy
archimate:Deliverable.documentation:
Iteratively develop an approved, baselined version of a technology strategy aligned with recognised market and government best practices.
1. Review emergent technology strategy, conceptual target architecture diagrams, and enterprise architecture domains e.g. business capabilities, high level reference architecture etc. 2. Characterise the current estate, define the problem statement, establish design principles, and outline a product-agnostic target state architecture. 3. Iteratively develop an approved, baselined version of a technology strategy aligned with recognised market and government best practices. 4. Define a proposed IT Product Structure aligned to the Technology Strategy to support ownership being defined. 5. For each functionally aligned Product, outline a proposed multi-year roadmap, outlining proposed scope of digital delivery. It should also consider and highlight any 'no regrets' sustainment activity to mitigate any operational or security risk to the estate to inform a 'sustainment strategy'. 6. Define the delineation of scope between the ICP Programme and the End of Life (EoL) project. 7. Define and characterise the integration approach/standard, and set out options to standardise application integration, maximising commercial portability, and minimising potential for lock-in.
Revised Technology strategy including strategic drivers, direction/objectives, design principles and conceptual target architecture for review and endorsement at Technical Design Authority. Engagement with senior stakeholders on the Technology Strategy for Homes England Endorsed Technology strategy for approval at Business Design Authority. Proposed functionally aligned IT product structure, to support ownership, with multi-year roadmaps. Proposed Business Service/Product Ownership structure. Proposed foundational integration standards and design to support technology strategy and product delivery, and definition of detailed requirements to support subsequent work to procure/build the capability.
